test_title: SSC Selection Post 2025 (Graduate Level) Official Paper (Held On: 24 Jul, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question:
Choose the **correct indirect speech** conversion of the sentence.

"Scientists say, 'Habits emerge because the brain is constantly looking for ways to save effort'".

options.text: Scientists say that habits emerge because the brain is constantly looking for ways to save effort.
Scientists said that habits emerged because the brain was constantly looking for ways to save effort.
Scientists say habits had emerged because the brain constantly looked for ways to save effort.
Scientists have said that habits emerge as the brain constantly looks for ways to save effort.

solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Indirect Speech:** Scientists say that habits emerge because the brain is constantly looking for ways to save effort.
 
• **Key Conversions:**
 
 
• **Reporting Verb in Present Tense:**
 
 
• The reporting verb **"say"** is in the present tense. According to grammar rules, if the reporting verb is in the present, future, or present perfect tense, the tense of the verbs in the reported speech does not change.
 
 
 
• **Universal Truth/Scientific Fact:**
 
 
• The statement *"Habits emerge because the brain is constantly looking for ways to save effort"* is a **scientific fact**. Scientific facts and general truths typically remain in the present tense when reported, even if the reporting verb is in the past tense.
 
 
 
• **Conjunction:**
 
 
• The conjunction **"that"** is used to introduce the reported clause in an assertive sentence.
 
 
 
 
 
• **Punctuation and Format:**
 
 
• Quotation marks and the comma following the reporting verb are removed.
 
• The sentence ends with a simple full stop.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"Scientists say that habits emerge because the brain is constantly looking for ways to save effort."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2:** "Scientists said that habits emerged because the brain was constantly looking for ways to save effort." 

 
 
• Incorrect because it unnecessarily changes the reporting verb to the past tense ("said") and shifts the scientific fact into the past tense ("emerged," "was looking").
 
 
 
• **Option 3:** "Scientists say habits had emerged because the brain constantly looked for ways to save effort." 
 
 
• Incorrect because it uses the past perfect ("had emerged") and simple past ("looked"), which alters the original meaning and violates the rule for present-tense reporting verbs.
 
 
 
• **Option 4:** "Scientists have said that habits emerge as the brain constantly looks for ways to save effort." 
 
 
• Incorrect because it changes the reporting verb to the present perfect ("have said") and modifies the original sentence structure (replacing "because" with "as").
